paper_metadata.title: Molecular dynamic study of temperature dependence of mechanical properties and plastic inception of CoCrCuFeNi high-entropy alloy

Three models are constructed by randomly position different alloying atoms at FCC lattice sites.
the model is initialized at 3000 K under an isothermal-isobaric (NPT) ensemble at 0 MPa pressure for 100 ps.
Then the model is quenched to 77 K at a cooling rate of 0.49 K/ps with a time step of 1 fs.
the energy minimization using the conjugate gradient algorithm is carried out with energy tolerance of 10−12 and force tolerance of 10−12 on Seed01.
Then the model is equilibrated using NPT ensemble at a pressure of 0 bar and a temperature of 77, 200, 300, 400, or 500 K.

After equilibrium, the model is deformed in uniaxial tension (z direction) at a constant strain rate of 1×108 with a stress-free condition in the other two (x and y) directions under the NPT ensemble.
It is observed that 69.9% atoms are arranged in FCC structure, indicating that FCC is the major crystalline phase of the CoCrCuFeNi HEA after quenching.
There are 17% atoms arranged in hexagonal close packed (HCP) structure and 13.1% atoms in amorphous.
There are 17% atoms arranged in hexagonal close packed (HCP) structure and 13.1% atoms in amorphous.
The results confirm that the potential can stabilize the CoCrCuFeNi HEA with an FCC phase at these temperatures.
Extensive intrinsic stacking faults (ISFs) and/or extrinsic stacking faults (ESFs) can be observed at all temperatures.
Extensive intrinsic stacking faults (ISFs) and/or extrinsic stacking faults (ESFs) can be observed at all temperatures. A deformation twin (DT) can be seen at 200 K.
A deformation twin (DT) can be seen at 200 K.
the ISF in Fig. 6a is formed by the emission of a leading 1/6[211] Shockley partial dislocation from the interior of the lattice.
The averaged τa of the CoCrCuFeNi HEA is 1.036, which is higher than that of pure Ni, Cu, and other common FCC metals [21]

At higher temperature, the lattice has higher entropy, which leads to the higher vibration amplitude of atoms as compared with that of the lattice at lower temperature. Therefore, bond breakage can readily occur at a higher temperature, resulting in a lower UTS.

The force gradient decreases under tensile strain, which implies that the stress increasing rate decreases with the tensile strain, explaining the elastic softening of the CoCrCuFeNi HEA under tensile strain.
Therefore, for the defect-free CoCrCuFeNi HEA, twins are homogeneously nucleated in the lattice by successive emissions of Shockley partial dislocations on adjacent (111) planes.

mechanisms.name: low stacking fault energy promoted twinning
